Factor smooth with a canonical null-space basis (bs = "fsc")

Source: R/smooth-fsc.R
smooth.construct.fsc.smooth.spec.Rd

A drop-in variant of mgcv's factor-smooth interaction (bs = "fs", see mgcv::factor.smooth) whose model matrix is stable under tiny (ulp-level) changes in the covariate. Use it as s(x, fac, bs = "fsc", k = ...); arguments xt, m and k behave as for "fs".

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fsc.smooth.spec'
smooth.construct(object, data, knots)

Arguments

object

A smooth specification object of class "fsc.smooth.spec", as produced by s(..., bs = "fsc").

data

A list or data frame containing the covariate and the factor.

knots

Optional list of knots, passed to the base smooth.

Value

A smooth object of class "fs.interaction", as returned by the "fs" constructor.

Details

The "fs" constructor reparameterises the base smooth with mgcv:::nat.param() and gives each of the null-space columns its own ridge penalty. For the usual second-order base smooth the null space is two-dimensional (constant and linear) and the two basis vectors that nat.param() returns for it span a degenerate eigenspace, so their orientation within that span is arbitrary and can rotate under a 1e-12 relative change in x. Because each column carries its own penalty, the rotation changes the fitted model, which makes criteria such as AIC discontinuous in the data.

"fsc" replaces those two columns with r * [1, (x - mean(x)) / sd(x)] – the same span in a fixed orientation, with r the root-mean-square size of the original null-space columns – and updates the reparameterisation matrix P to match, so the "fs" prediction method (mgcv::Predict.matrix() for class "fs.interaction") reproduces the fit on new data. Column space, penalty structure and number of smoothing parameters are those of "fs". When the null space of the base smooth is not two-dimensional, the smooth is not one-dimensional, or the canonical columns are not in the null-space span, the result is plain "fs".

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = runif(90, 40, 80), f = factor(rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 30)))
d$y <- sin(d$x / 10) + as.numeric(d$f) + rnorm(90, 0, 0.2)
fit <- mgcv::gam(y ~ s(x, f, bs = "fsc", k = 5), data = d, method = "REML")
